mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates and increases equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC (FEDFUNDS vs 20d returns) is greater than -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.3 percentage points over a 3-month period signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes economic slowdowns and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances or Rank IC (UNRATE change vs 20d returns) > -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and low unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals late-cycle monetary tightening that increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.2pp in 3 months and UNRATE < 4.0%
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances or Rank IC for interaction signal > -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 2% in one month signals weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances during late-cycle expansions or Rank IC (HOUST change vs 20d returns) > -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals robust economic activity that supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC (INDPRO vs 5d returns) < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 2.5% signals persistent inflation that typically prompts Federal Reserve tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% (YoY) or Rank IC (CPIAUCSL YoY vs 20d returns) < -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous deceleration in employment growth (PAYEMS) and increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a deteriorating labor market that often precedes economic slowdowns, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth rate declines > 0.5% in 3 months AND UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances or Rank IC for interaction signal > -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a decline in quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) exceeding 0.5% signals weakening economic momentum that typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate declines > 0.5% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances during late-cycle expansions or Rank IC (GDPC1 growth vs 60d returns) > -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
